drill.q: Severe ARDS, PEEP 5→10, MAP falls 65→45. More PEEP is least likely to help in which setting?
drill.a: RV dysfunction: PEEP raises PVR. RV-protective ventilation = low plateau/driving pressure, correct PaO₂ and PaCO₂, prone.

drill.q: Eisenmenger syndrome: treatment, and the two things you never do?
drill.a: Bosentan (BREATHE-5; PDE-5 inhibitor as alternative). Never close the defect; never a calcium channel blocker (↓SVR → more right-to-left shunt).

drill.q: Dilated RV, CVP 20, hypotension, distended abdomen. Massive PE or chronic RV failure from PH?
drill.a: Chronic RV failure from PH: ascites needs time (one in three chose massive PE). An RV free wall >5 mm would confirm chronicity.

drill.q: CT main pulmonary artery diameter that suggests pulmonary hypertension?
drill.a: >3 cm before the bifurcation, or PA:aorta ratio >1 (55% right). Confirm with echo, then right heart catheter.

drill.q: Inferior STEMI, hypotension, raised JVP, clear lungs: which ECG finding means RV involvement, and what do you give?
drill.a: ST elevation III > II (also V1, and ≥1 mm in V4R). Normal saline bolus; avoid nitrates and diuretics.

drill.q: PAPi: formula and the cut-off in inferior MI?
drill.a: (PA systolic − PA diastolic) / RA pressure. <0.9 predicts RV failure and in-hospital death (Marrow: PAPi 0.4 carried the greatest mortality).

drill.q: Echo cut-offs for RV overload: TAPSE, FAC, TR velocity?
drill.a: TAPSE <17 mm, FAC <35%, TR velocity >2.8 m/s; RV ≥ LV; IVC distended with <50% collapse. Thick wall = chronic.

drill.q: McConnell's sign: what is it, and which sign is more specific for PE versus RV infarction?
drill.a: RV free-wall hypokinesia with apical sparing (NEET 2025). The 60/60 sign: PA acceleration time <60 ms with TR gradient <60 mmHg (DocT GT).

drill.q: PE with RV strain, raised troponin, BP 96/58. Thrombolyse?
drill.a: No. Intermediate-high risk: anticoagulate and monitor, rescue lysis only if decompensation. Hypotension (SBP <90) decides lysis: alteplase 100 mg over 2 h (GT4 Q26; INI-SS).

drill.q: Wells score: signs of DVT + PE most likely + HR 110 + surgery 2 weeks ago = ?
drill.a: 3 + 3 + 1.5 + 1.5 = 9 (GT8 Q10). >4 = PE likely → CTPA without D-dimer.

drill.q: Wells items worth 1.5 points, and those worth 1?
drill.a: 1.5: HR >100; immobilisation ≥3 days or surgery within 4 weeks; previous DVT/PE. 1: haemoptysis; cancer.

drill.q: D-dimer cut-off for a 70-year-old? Isolated subsegmental PE, no proximal DVT, low recurrence risk?
drill.a: 700 µg/L (age × 10 above 50 years). Clinical surveillance with repeat leg ultrasound, no anticoagulation (CHEST 2021; 17% right).

drill.q: 3 h after mitral repair: hypotension, hypoxia, dilated hypokinetic RV, preserved LV, high CVP. Next step?
drill.a: Start inhaled nitric oxide (67–71%). Not fluids, not more PEEP, not high-dose furosemide.

drill.q: Inhaled NO: primary goal, dose, and what to do for rebound hypoxia after stopping it?
drill.a: Reduce PVR (in ventilated lung only). Start 5 ppm, range 20–40 ppm. Restart and wean slowly to about 1 ppm before stopping (Marrow).

drill.q: IPAH on IV epoprostenol admitted with RV failure: the one rule, and the keyed 'additional therapy'?
drill.a: Never interrupt epoprostenol (rebound PH crisis). DocT keyed lifelong anticoagulation (64%); ESC/ERS 2022 individualises it.

drill.q: Shock within hours of heart transplant: least likely cause?
drill.a: Acute cellular (T-cell) rejection: days to weeks. Likely: primary graft dysfunction, RV failure against recipient PH, tamponade (only 23% right).

traps.trap: True RV failure is a raised CVP with normal RV function
traps.truth: That is volume. Failure = RV dysfunction plus limited filling (high CVP, inadequate forward flow).

traps.trap: RV failure is increased RV filling without a fall in output
traps.truth: If output is maintained the RV is coping; failure is when filling rises and stroke volume does not follow.

traps.trap: RV stroke work equals LV stroke work because the stroke volume is the same
traps.truth: Work = volume × pressure; RV stroke work is about a quarter of the LV's.

traps.trap: The RV tolerates preload, so keep giving fluid in RV failure
traps.truth: Only up to a point: then annular dilatation, TR and septal shift lower LV filling and output.

traps.trap: Aortic regurgitation causes a high LA pressure with a low LVEDV
traps.truth: AR raises LVEDV. High LAP with a small LV = septal shift from PH, high PEEP or severe hypoxaemic respiratory failure.

traps.trap: Pulsus paradoxus in tamponade is from blood pooling in the lungs
traps.truth: Inspiratory RV filling shifts the septum left inside a fixed pericardium, so LV filling falls.

traps.trap: The RV is afterload tolerant because it already works against a low resistance
traps.truth: That is why it has no reserve: stroke volume falls steeply as mPAP rises 0–30 mmHg.

traps.trap: Hypotensive RV failure: fluids first, vasopressors later
traps.truth: Hypotension removes RV coronary perfusion; restore aortic pressure early, and fluid may worsen dilatation.

traps.trap: PH is mPAP >25 mmHg (card and DocT key)
traps.truth: ESC/ERS 2022: mPAP >20, PAWP ≤15, PVR >2 WU for pre-capillary PH. Choose >20 if offered; >25 only if it is the sole pressure option beside a high wedge/LVEDP.

traps.trap: A PVR below 3 WU fits PAH
traps.truth: PAH needs a raised PVR, now >2 WU.

traps.trap: Young woman, Raynaud's, JVD, oedema, loud P2: left heart failure, ILD or CTEPH
traps.truth: Raynaud's → systemic sclerosis → group 1 PAH; no orthopnoea or crackles, no VTE history.

traps.trap: Raised mPAP with a normal wedge always means group 1 PAH
traps.truth: It means pre-capillary (groups 1, 3, 4, 5). With antiphospholipid syndrome the cause is recurrent PE (group 4).

traps.trap: Syncope is the commonest symptom of PH
traps.truth: Exertional dyspnoea is; syncope is a late high-risk sign.

traps.trap: A massive saddle PE is the commonest embolic cause of chronic PH
traps.truth: Multiple small recurrent emboli; air and fat emboli are acute events.

traps.trap: Old PE, PA thrombus, severe PH: WHO group 1
traps.truth: Chronic thromboembolic PH is group 4.

traps.trap: Anticoagulated hypoxaemic CTEPH, mPAP 40: IV epoprostenol next (Marrow key)
traps.truth: Guideline ladder: endarterectomy if operable → balloon angioplasty → riociguat; epoprostenol only for the critically ill. Mark the key only if PEA and riociguat are not offered.

traps.trap: ARVC with woolly hair and keratoderma is Carvajal syndrome
traps.truth: Naxos is the RV-dominant ARVC syndrome; Carvajal has the same skin and hair with a dilated LV.

traps.trap: More PEEP is least likely to help in severe ARDS or obesity
traps.truth: Those patients usually recruit; the keyed answer is RV dysfunction, where PEEP raises PVR.

traps.trap: Prone positioning is only an oxygenation manoeuvre
traps.truth: It also unloads the RV by lowering PVR and airway pressures.

traps.trap: Eisenmenger syndrome: start a calcium channel blocker, beta-blocker or digoxin, or close the defect
traps.truth: Bosentan (BREATHE-5). CCBs increase the right-to-left shunt; closure removes the RV's vent.

traps.trap: Acute dyspnoea + hypotension + dilated RV + CVP 20 + distended abdomen = massive PE
traps.truth: Ascites needs time: chronic RV failure from pulmonary hypertension.

traps.trap: A main PA above 2 cm (or only above 4–5 cm) suggests PH
traps.truth: About 3 cm on CT (or PA:aorta >1).

traps.trap: ST elevation in II greater than III means RV involvement
traps.truth: III > II (with V1 and V4R) points to the RCA and RV; II > III points to the circumflex.

traps.trap: S1Q3T3 is the RV infarct pattern
traps.truth: It is the RV strain (PE) pattern, and it is insensitive.

traps.trap: The lowest cardiac index best predicts death in RV-infarct shock
traps.truth: PAPi <0.9 does (the stem's PAPi was 0.4).

traps.trap: Echo confirms pulmonary hypertension
traps.truth: Echo gives a probability; right heart catheterisation confirms.

traps.trap: McConnell's sign is the most specific finding for PE versus RV infarction
traps.truth: RV infarction copies it; the 60/60 sign is more specific.

traps.trap: A D-shaped LV, low TAPSE, or effusion with RV collapse points to PE
traps.truth: The first two mean RV overload of any cause; RV collapse is tamponade.

traps.trap: PE with RV strain and troponin, BP 96/58: thrombolyse
traps.truth: Intermediate-high risk: anticoagulate and monitor. Only hypotension (SBP <90), shock or arrest earns systemic lysis.

traps.trap: Wells score added to 6 for DVT signs + PE most likely + HR >100 + recent surgery
traps.truth: 3 + 3 + 1.5 + 1.5 = 9. Score all seven items; HR, immobility/surgery and previous VTE are 1.5 each.

traps.trap: Anticoagulate every subsegmental PE
traps.truth: Isolated, no proximal DVT, low recurrence risk: clinical surveillance with repeat leg ultrasound (CHEST 2021).

traps.trap: Aggressive fluids, more PEEP or high-dose furosemide for a dilated RV with high CVP after mitral repair
traps.truth: Start inhaled nitric oxide to lower PVR.

traps.trap: IPAH on epoprostenol in RV failure: CCB trial, rapid diuresis or digoxin
traps.truth: Never interrupt epoprostenol; decongest gently; keyed add-on was lifelong anticoagulation (disputed under ESC/ERS 2022).

traps.trap: Nitrates or diuretics for inferior STEMI with hypotension and clear lungs
traps.truth: RV infarct with normal afterload is preload dependent: fluid bolus.

traps.trap: IV furosemide dose lower than the home oral dose
traps.truth: At least equal to the oral dose (ESC 2021: 1–2 times).

traps.trap: Levosimendan loading bolus with SBP 85
traps.truth: The bolus is optional and not recommended if SBP <90 mmHg.

traps.trap: Inhaled NO is given to raise systemic BP or improve surfactant
traps.truth: Its goal is to reduce PVR.

traps.trap: Hypoxia after stopping inhaled NO: 100% oxygen and wait
traps.truth: Rebound PH: restart NO and wean slowly to about 1 ppm.

traps.trap: A micro-axial pump also oxygenates
traps.truth: Only ECMO, or an RVAD with an added oxygenator, supports gas exchange.

traps.trap: Shock hours after heart transplant: PH or tamponade is the least likely cause
traps.truth: Both are common early; acute cellular (T-cell) rejection takes days to weeks.

mimics.pair: RV failure vs RV dysfunction
mimics.tell: Failure adds a high CVP and inadequate forward flow; dysfunction alone has normal filling pressures.

mimics.pair: RV failure vs hypervolaemia
mimics.tell: High CVP with a normally contracting RV is volume and settles with diuresis.

mimics.pair: Septal shift vs primary LV disease (both high LA pressure)
mimics.tell: Septal shift gives a small LV (low LVEDV); LV disease or AR gives a normal or large one.

mimics.pair: Volume vs pressure overload on the septum
mimics.tell: Flattening in diastole only = volume; persisting into systole = pressure.

mimics.pair: PAH (group 1) vs PH of left heart disease (group 2)
mimics.tell: PAWP ≤15 vs >15 mmHg.

mimics.pair: CTD-associated PAH vs ILD-associated PH in systemic sclerosis
mimics.tell: PAH has clear lungs; ILD has crackles and fibrosis on CT.

mimics.pair: CTEPH (group 4) vs PAH (group 1)
mimics.tell: Mismatched perfusion defects on V/Q scan (normal V/Q excludes CTEPH).

mimics.pair: Naxos vs Carvajal
mimics.tell: Same woolly hair and keratoderma; Naxos is RV-dominant ARVC, Carvajal a dilated LV.

mimics.pair: ARVC vs RVOT tachycardia (both LBBB-morphology VT)
mimics.tell: ARVC has a structurally abnormal RV with T inversion V1–V3 or epsilon waves; RVOT VT has a normal heart.

mimics.pair: PEEP hypotension from RV afterload vs from low preload
mimics.tell: Afterload: RV dilates and the septum flattens; preload: both ventricles small and empty.

mimics.pair: Chronic RV failure from PH vs massive PE
mimics.tell: Time: ascites, anasarca or an RV wall >5 mm means chronic; a thin dilated RV is acute.

mimics.pair: RV failure vs tamponade (both raised JVP, hypotension, pulsus paradoxus)
mimics.tell: Right chambers large in RV failure; small and collapsing in tamponade.

mimics.pair: Big PA with clear lungs vs big PA with oedema
mimics.tell: Oedema means the left heart is driving the PH (group 2).

mimics.pair: RV infarction vs RV strain on ECG
mimics.tell: Infarct: ST elevation V4R, III > II with an inferior STEMI. Strain: T inversion V1–V4, S1Q3T3.

mimics.pair: Isolated RV failure vs biventricular failure on the catheter
mimics.tell: CVP > PCWP in isolated RV failure.

mimics.pair: PE vs RV infarction on echo
mimics.tell: 60/60 sign (acceleration time <60 ms, TR gradient <60 mmHg) is PE; McConnell's sign occurs in both.

mimics.pair: McConnell's sign vs Takotsubo
mimics.tell: McConnell: RV free wall still, RV apex moves. Takotsubo: LV apex balloons, base vigorous.

mimics.pair: Intermediate-high vs high-risk PE
mimics.tell: Hypotension (SBP <90), shock or arrest. Both have RV dysfunction and troponin.

mimics.pair: Wells vs Daniel score tachycardia
mimics.tell: HR >100 scores 1.5 in Wells (clinical probability) and 2 in Daniel (ECG strain).

mimics.pair: RV infarction vs PE/PH: fluid or not
mimics.tell: PVR: normal in RV infarct (fluid helps), high in PE and PH (fluid harms).

mimics.pair: Dobutamine vs levosimendan
mimics.tell: Levosimendan is a calcium sensitiser that also dilates pulmonary vessels; dobutamine is a short-acting β-agonist.

mimics.pair: Inhaled vs IV pulmonary vasodilators
mimics.tell: Inhaled act only in ventilated lung: oxygenation improves, no hypotension. IV dilate everything.

mimics.pair: ECMO vs surgical RVAD
mimics.tell: ECMO: fast, oxygenates, days. RVAD: weeks to months, needs an added oxygenator.

mimics.pair: Primary graft dysfunction vs acute cellular rejection
mimics.tell: Timing: within 24 hours vs days to weeks.

new_cards.why: GT8 Q10 (missed): Wells score 9 = signs of DVT 3 + PE most likely 3 + HR >100 1.5 + recent surgery 1.5. CAR-24 gives the D-dimer, subsegmental PE and Daniel score but not the Wells items.

card_flags.issue: Part a gives 2–9% of acute heart failure admissions; the source usually quoted (ESC/HFA acute RV failure statement, Harjola 2016) and card RVF-02 give 3–9%. Suggest 3–9%.

Defines PH as mean PA pressure >25 mmHg (and labels it 'MAP'). ESC/ERS 2022: mPAP >20 mmHg; pre-capillary adds PAWP ≤15 and PVR >2 WU. DocT still keys >25. Chronic haemolytic anaemia is listed under group 1; it is in group 5. Suggest updating and adding the PAWP/PVR line.

Group 5 list is the older one: splenectomy, vasculitis, thyroid disorders and congenital heart disease are no longer in group 5 (ESC/ERS 2022: haematological, systemic, metabolic, chronic renal failure, tumour thrombotic microangiopathy, fibrosing mediastinitis). Group 4 line ('high blood pressure, blood clots') is vague; suggest adding V/Q screening and the PEA → BPA → riociguat ladder.
TGA is filed under volume overload; a systemic RV (atrial-switch d-TGA, ccTGA) is mainly pressure loaded. Low exam relevance.

Part a reads 'enlarged main PA and regional oligaemia → pulmonary oedema; clear lung fields', which is self-contradictory. Isolated RV failure has clear lung fields; oedema means left heart disease. Suggest adding the asked CT cut-off (main PA >3 cm, PA:aorta >1).
Lacks PAPi, which Marrow asked: (PASP − PADP)/RAP, <0.9 in inferior MI predicts RV failure and death (<1.85 after LVAD). Suggest adding one line.
Says only 'seen in PE'. DocT GT keys the 60/60 sign as more specific than McConnell's sign for PE versus RV infarction. Suggest adding that McConnell's also occurs in RV infarction.

Volume loading '>200 mL / 15–30 min' is the HFA/ESC 2016 acute RV failure statement figure (Harjola); ESC 2019 PE says cautious loading of ≤500 mL over 15–30 min. Both taught; suggest noting the 500 mL cap.

Lists hypotension and hypoxia as adverse effects of inhaled prostaglandins; these belong mainly to IV prostacyclin (inhaled is largely selective). Card also lacks the asked fact: abrupt iNO withdrawal causes rebound PH (wean to 1 ppm).

Lists IABP as mechanical support for RV failure; it has little role for the RV (RVF-43 does not list it). DocT's 'lifelong anticoagulation in IPAH on epoprostenol' key is not supported by ESC/ERS 2022 (individualised).

Lacks the Wells score, asked at GT8 Q10 (missed). New card V12-040 written; the items are taught in this step's lesson. Daniel score '≥10 = severe pulmonary hypertension' is better read as systolic PA pressure above about 50 mmHg.

No error. Note for currency: the 2026 AHA/ACC acute PE guideline (JACC 2026) introduces clinical categories A–E (A subclinical to E cardiopulmonary failure) alongside the ESC classes; advanced therapy is reserved for the higher categories. NEET keys the ESC classes.
